blocks.text: I can describe simple properties of {solids}, {liquids} and {gases}.
In this lesson you will find out about the states of matter and what makes each one different.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.
A solid has a fixed shape and volume but some solids can change shape when a force is applied.
A liquid can flow, has a fixed volume and takes the shape of the bottom of its container.
A gas can flow, has no fixed volume and takes the shape of the whole of its container.
The properties of a material or substance are its qualities or things it can do.

blocks.text: A **material** is the substance that objects are made from, such as wood, metal or plastic.
Materials are used to make objects such as tables, cars and books.
The word ‘material’ comes from the word ‘matter’. Both words refer to what objects are made from.
The substances that materials are made from can exist as different **states of matter**.
Water can exist in the solid, liquid or gas state.
The **properties** of a material or substance are its qualities or things it can do.
Solids, liquids and gases have different {properties}.
This means that one substance can behave in different ways depending on what state it is in.
Once we know these properties, we can spot solids, liquids and gases.
Imagine three balloons. One contains solid water (ice), one contains liquid water and one contains gas (air).
Press each balloon, then cut the knot off and try to empty the contents into a bowl. What happens?

blocks.label: Tap to see one class’s results
blocks.text: When they pressed the balloons, they could change the shape of the gas balloon and the liquid balloon, but not the solid one.

blocks.label: Tap to see what happened in the bowl
blocks.text: The **solid** did not flow into the bowl and the ice stayed the same shape. The **liquid** flowed into the bowl and took the shape of the bottom of the bowl. They couldn’t see the **gas**, but it escaped out into the room because the balloon was no longer inflated.
A liquid can be poured easily and takes the shape of the bottom of its container.
Even when liquids change their shape, they always take up the same amount of space. This is called **volume**.
This means that liquids have a {fixed volume}.
Imagine four containers of different shapes, each holding the same volume of coloured water. The containers are different shapes, but there is the same amount of liquid in each one.

blocks.q: Water is poured from a tall, thin jug into a wide bowl. Which property of the water stays the same?
options: how much space it takes up (its volume)
blocks.why: Liquids have a fixed volume. The shape changes to fit the container, but the amount of space the liquid takes up stays the same.

blocks.text: Solids have many different appearances and properties.

items: Solids have a fixed shape, but some solids can change shape when a force is applied.
Solids have a fixed volume. They always take up the same amount of space.
Solids do not flow like liquids.

blocks.text: Gases can be tricky to understand because they are often invisible to the human eye, but we can feel them.
Move your hand from side to side quickly. You can feel the air, but you cannot see it.

items: Gases can flow, even though we can usually not see them.
They spread out to fill the container they are in and take the shape of the whole container.
If their container is not sealed, gases can escape and spread out, so they do not have a fixed shape or volume.

blocks.text: Air is a mixture of gases, including nitrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide. All of them are in the gas state.

items.title: oxygen
items.sub: animals, including humans, need it to survive

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Just because we usually cannot see a gas does not mean it is not there. Gases are materials in the gas state and they have properties too.

items.q: A container of gas is left open (not sealed). What happens to the gas?
options: It stays exactly where it is

items.q: Which state of matter has no fixed volume?
A wooden block keeps its shape. That is because wood is in the ... state.

blocks.q: Is each property of a solid, a liquid or a gas?

items.text: keeps its shape unless a force changes it
takes the shape of the bottom of its container
takes the shape of the whole container

blocks.q: Match each material to its state of matter.

items: Substances can exist as different states of matter: solid, liquid and gas.
Solids, liquids and gases have different properties.
Liquids can be poured easily and take the shape of the bottom of the container that they are in.
A solid has a fixed shape and volume, but some solids can change shape when a force is applied.
Gases are often invisible to the human eye. They escape from an unsealed container and have no fixed shape or volume.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Properties of solids, liquids and gases
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a short answer. Use what you learned about the properties of solids, liquids and gases.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter has no fixed shape or volume?
questions.explanation: A gas spreads out to fill its container, so it has no fixed shape or volume.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter can be poured easily and takes the shape of the bottom of its container?
questions.explanation: Liquids can be poured easily and take the shape of the bottom of their container.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter keeps its shape unless a force changes it?
questions.explanation: A solid has a fixed shape, although some solids can change shape when a force is applied.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter fills any sealed container that it is in?
questions.explanation: Gases spread out to fill the container they are in and take the shape of the whole container.

questions.prompt: Which two states of matter have a fixed volume?
questions.explanation: Solids and liquids always take up the same amount of space. Gases do not have a fixed volume.

questions.prompt: How many common states of matter are there?
questions.explanation: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.

questions.prompt: Solids, liquids and gases have different what? (The qualities of a material or things it can do.)
questions.explanation: The properties of a material are its qualities or things it can do, and they are different in each state.
Water in the solid state is ice.

questions.prompt: Oxygen in the air is in which state of matter?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a gas, and air is a mixture of gases.
